english.title: Aiding prisoner to attempt to escape from prison establishment
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) aided **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), a prisoner, in attempting to escape from

(A)_[His Majesty's prison at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..)]_
(B)_[His Majesty's remand centre at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..) being an institution to which section 43 of the Prison Act 1952 applied]_
(C)_[His Majesty's young offenders institution at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..) being an institution to which section 43 of the Prison Act 1952 applied]_
(D)_[His Majesty's secure training centre at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..) being an institution to which section 43 of the Prison Act 1952 applied]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 39 of the Prison Act 1952.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
aided prisoner
to attempt to escape
from prison/remand centre/young offenders institution/secure training centre

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This Standard Offence Wording is obsolete as from 31st March 2008. Repealed by the Offender Management Act 2007.
(ii) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.

other.penalty:
Indictment: maximum 10 years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
